gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Noto Sans Adlam stands its lowercase c, s and z tall and full. Curve endings stay well apart, so paragraphs of it read without clotting, while Origami keeps its marker-traced single stroke for the headline.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Monoline swagger on top, restraint underneath. Origami is best at bold single-stroke display lettering, while Noto Sans Lisu does its best work in text, with wide-open s curves and tiny ascender gaps.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-saira: Glass-tube lettering over rounded sans-serif type. Make Origami small and its hollow tube lettering fades away, while Saira keeps its see-through s and tall rounded letters happily at text size.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sarpanch: Cord-like curves, tidy little letters. Origami's curves weigh the same as its stems, like cord, while Sarpanch keeps a clearly open e and compact lines, so running text moves along easily.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sulphur-point: Brushy heading, bulky, marker-weighted body. What stands out is how Origami's single-stroke brush line is echoed by Sulphur Point's steady, marker-like weight, with distinct open gaps inside its letters.
